about: Every setting VPX 10.9.0 build 7001 declares (src/core/Settings_properties.inl, its add-ons' MSGPI_*_SETTING declarations), the classic VPinMAME's for every machine and the app's own, for the app's Advanced page. Generated by tools/settings-map/settings_map.py: edit that and tools/settings-map/status.json, not this file.

categories.label: Windows and screens
categories.note: Where each window goes, its screen and size; the cabinet's screens and where the player stands.

categories.label: Picture
categories.note: How tables are drawn: quality, effects, the ball, light, smoothing and frame timing.

categories.label: Score displays
categories.note: The looks of dot-matrix and segment displays, VPX's profiles.

categories.label: Sound
categories.note: The sound outputs, the speaker layout and the volumes.

categories.label: Controls, nudging and plunger
categories.note: The tilt bob, the nudge and the plunger.

categories.label: Physics
categories.note: VPX's physics sets, which a table's own can be swapped for.

categories.label: Table overrides and camera
categories.note: Settings that count over every table's own, and the camera tables open with.

categories.label: Plugins
categories.note: The settings of VPX's own add-ons: its PinMAME, backglass, PinUP, DMD, colour, sound and toy add-ons.

categories.label: VPinMAME, every machine
categories.note: The classic VPinMAME's settings for every machine, kept where it keeps them, in your part of Windows' registry (a game's own, on its table's settings, count over these).

categories.label: Visual Pinball Infinite's own
categories.note: Ours, in the [VPI] section: what VPX hasn't.

categories.label: The player, other
categories.note: VPX's other settings: logs, debugging, its profiles, and VPinMAME's older backglass and toy switches.

categories.label: VPX's editor
categories.note: VPX's table editor's settings and the defaults it gives new parts.

None: No synchronization. Vertical Sync: Synchronize on video sync, avoids video tearing at the price of high visual latency. Adaptive Sync: Synchronize on video sync, except for late frames (below target FPS), also features higher visual latency. Frame Pacing: pace the frame rendering to limit visual latency, comes with the risk of introducing more stutters if the computer is not powerful enough.
-1 will limit FPS to the display refresh rate 0 will not limit the display refresh rate Other values will limit the FPS to it (energy saving/less heat, framerate stability)

Maximum number of 'frames in flight' (frames pushed to the GPU queue waiting for rendering). Higher values may lead to higher FPS, but at higher input latency. Recommended to be adjusted to the lowest value that allows a stable framerate. (Not supported in OpenGL version)

settings.d: Whether a sound plays as each achievement is announced: the pack's own, or the player's chime (Settings › Sound).
The level of the sound played as an achievement is announced, over the backglass volume, from 0 to 2: one of the pause menu's sound levels (Settings › Sound too).

Where a card shows as each achievement is earned, its picture, name and points over what that window shows; VPX's own notice on the playfield, as VPX lets add-ons draw only in its other windows, and wherever the chosen window isn't showing (Settings › Screens).
How wide the achievement popup's card is: small, medium or large, about two fifths, three fifths or four fifths of its window's width (Settings › Screens).

settings.l: The screens layout tables play with
settings.d: One of the Screens page's saved layouts, by its name; a table's own settings can name another.

settings.l: A screenshot at a high score
settings.d: A screenshot when a game makes the high scores — a ROM machine's in its memory, or a table script's own when it saves a new one — into the table's screenshots.
The windows a screenshot takes: playfield, backglass, dmd and topper, separated by commas; empty, every window that shows.

settings.l: Tables may reach outside their files
settings.d: Tables' scripts may reach outside their own files — the internet, other programs, every file — as some tables' online features need; off, each script keeps to its table's own files. A table's own line in a [ScriptsReachOutside] section, its file's name = 1 or 0, counts over this for that table.
The folder holding the library's tables, which first setup sets; the app and the player read the library from it.
The folder of the scripts tables load (core.vbs, controller.vbs and the machines' own); empty, the Scripts folder beside the tables folder.
The folder holding the library's PinUP packs (PinUP's PUPVideos); empty, the one found above the tables.

settings.l: How the library keeps its tables
settings.d: game: each game in a folder of its own, its versions sharing it, as Visual Pinball X 10.8.1 keeps tables; empty, VPX's shared folders. The app's Library settings switch between them, moving the files.

The folder holding Future Pinball's program, its tables played in it through BAM; empty, looked for beside VPX's folder, where its installer put it, and in its usual folders. Settings › Library says where it was found.

settings.l: The VR program VPX plays with
settings.d: The OpenXR manifest of the VR program VPX plays VR with, for its games alone (Meta Horizon Link's, SteamVR's, Virtual Desktop's); empty, the one Windows has active. Settings › VR chooses it among those found.

settings.l: The headset's resolution with Meta Horizon Link
settings.d: VPX's [PlayerVR] ResFactor while it plays VR through Meta Horizon Link: each eye drawn at the size Link recommends times this, past 0.1 and up to 10; empty, Link's own size. Settings › VR keeps one for each VR program, so one chosen for another isn't carried over.

VPX's [PlayerVR] ResFactor while it plays VR through SteamVR: each eye drawn at the size SteamVR recommends times this, past 0.1 and up to 10; empty, SteamVR's own size. Settings › VR keeps one for each VR program.

settings.l: The headset's resolution with Virtual Desktop
settings.d: VPX's [PlayerVR] ResFactor while it plays VR through Virtual Desktop: each eye drawn at the size Virtual Desktop recommends for its graphics quality times this, past 0.1 and up to 10; empty, Virtual Desktop's own size. Settings › VR keeps one for each VR program.

settings.l: The headset's resolution with Pimax Play
settings.d: VPX's [PlayerVR] ResFactor while it plays VR through Pimax Play: each eye drawn at the size it recommends times this, past 0.1 and up to 10; empty, its own size. Settings › VR keeps one for each VR program.

settings.l: The headset's resolution with Varjo Base
settings.d: VPX's [PlayerVR] ResFactor while it plays VR through Varjo Base: each eye drawn at the size it recommends times this, past 0.1 and up to 10; empty, its own size. Settings › VR keeps one for each VR program.

settings.l: The headset's resolution with another VR program
settings.d: VPX's [PlayerVR] ResFactor while it plays VR through any other VR program: each eye drawn at the size it recommends times this, past 0.1 and up to 10; empty, its own size. Settings › VR keeps one for each VR program.

settings.l: The VPX that plays the tables
settings.d: 10.8.0: Visual Pinball X 10.8.0 plays the tables where it's kept beside a newer one; empty, the newest found. Settings › Library chooses it, after a window comparing the two.
The folder Visual Pinball X's programs are in, where it isn't the one above the tables (Settings › Library's Choose VPX's folder).

settings.l: The screenshot key while VPX plays
settings.d: F1, F2, F4 to F9, or Off: the key screenshots of each of VPX's windows are taken with while Visual Pinball X 10.8.1 plays a table the app started (Settings › Controls).
Where PinballX is installed, for putting a table's media where it shows them; empty, its usual folders are looked in.
Where PinballY is installed, for putting a table's media where it shows them; empty, its usual folders are looked in.
